## Description and Rationale

The team south-wind is a solo project run by a data analyst with several
years of experience in data analytics and machine learning. After
working in larger tech hubs, the participant now lives in Haikou, a
coastal city on the south coast of Hainan Island, China, and works
locally. The name "south-wind" comes from this setting: doing aviation
research from a small coastal city in the south, where the south wind
blows year-round.

The team joined the PRC Data Challenge 2026 for three reasons:

1. To learn and sharpen skills in time-series regression and gradient
   boosting modelling. Predicting taxi-out time is a concrete,
   well-scoped problem that is ideal for practising feature
   engineering, time-series validation and ensemble methods.

2. To contribute to open aviation research. Even if the final ranking   is modest, the team plans to release all code and notes under an
   open licence so that future participants can build on this work.

3. To do something useful and a bit different. Aviation operations
   have real-world impact on emissions and passenger experience, and
   being able to predict taxi-out time even roughly is genuinely
   useful. Working on it from the south wind side of the world is the
   team's small way to participate in open European aviation research.

The team will work primarily in Python, using XGBoost, LightGBM and
CatBoost as the main models, with feature engineering focused on
time-of-day, congestion patterns and aircraft-specific factors.
